subject: general
question:
Three Statements are given followed by Four conclusions numbered I, II, III and IV. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some copies are pillows.

Some pillows are laptops.

Some laptops are pens.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some copies are laptops.

II. Some pillows are pens.

III. Some pens are laptops.

IV. Some pens are pillows.
solution:
**Given:**

Statements:

Some copies are pillows.

Some pillows are laptops.

Some laptops are pens.

The least possible Venn diagram for the statement given is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b469a7298a615af2486400e0debaade91e91a6cf5fe9cab689c8d8b9264750ba.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some copies are laptops. → **False **(There is not any definite relation is given between Copies and Laptops. So, it can be possible only.)

II. Some pillows are pens. → **False **(There is not any definite relation is given between pillows and pens. So, it can be possible only.)

III. Some pens are laptops. → **True **(It is given that some laptop are pen so it simply means that some pen are laptop.)

IV. Some pens are pillows. → **False **(There is not any definite relation is given between pens and pillows. So, it can be possible only.)

So, only** conclusion III** follows.

Hence, the correct answer is ***'Option 4'.***
